BIM log mining for interactive target value design
abstract: Even with building information modeling (BIM) adoption, early-stage cost and schedule estimation requires a round-trip to external tools or specialists, decoupling assessment from design iteration. Such delayed assessment breaks the early feedback needed for target value design (TVD), limiting designers’ ability to respond early to emerging cost and schedule overruns. This study proposes an artificial intelligence (AI)-augmented BIM log mining framework that facilitates interactive TVD, focusing on cost and schedule. The proposed framework comprises three modules: (1) element-level state logging; (2) cost and schedule estimation using shape-constrained machine learning regressors; and (3) in-authoring visualization of estimation trajectories. Validation on 94 projects shows mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) of 28.5% for cost and 15.4% for schedule. The proposed t-dependent origin anchoring transformation addresses low-count extrapolation violations, yielding logically consistent estimates for early design states that are underrepresented during training. State-log-based feature updates keep interactive latency below 100 milliseconds, providing immediate feedback.

Human–AI collaboration in architectural design: Interaction, design process and controllability
abstract: This review article examines the integration of artificial intelligence (AI) in architectural design, focusing on human–AI collaboration, interaction, design stages, input–output data exchange, and human controllability. Despite recent advances, existing reviews emphasize application domains, offering limited insight into how responsibility, decision-making, and controllability are distributed between designers and AI systems. Such insight is essential for developing decision support systems, enabling progression from early design stages toward construction documentation, and reducing the gap between computer-aided design and construction. To address this gap, a PRISMA-based review of 96 journal and conference papers was conducted. The findings identify four dominant collaboration modes, with Human-on-the-Loop being the most prevalent. AI applications remain concentrated in schematic design, with limited but emerging engagement in later phases. Image-based data dominates inputs and outputs despite limited precision and editability. The review shows that collaboration mode and information embedded in the design process shape human controllability over AI-generated outcomes.

abstract: Since 2022, advances in Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Large Language Models (LLMs) have reshaped Automated Compliance Checking (ACC) in AEC. This review applies an AI-driven PRISMA workflow combining LLM-assisted discovery and screening with transparent provenance and audit trails. Studies are mapped to five ACC pipeline stages: rule interpretation, model preparation, rule execution, reporting, and decision support. Iterative coding identifies ten cross-cutting themes used as analytical lenses: Multimodal Information Extraction, Formalisation of Regulatory Text, Semantic Alignment with BIM/IFC, Integration of Ontologies and Knowledge Graphs, Rule Representation and Reasoning, Model-Driven Compliance Intelligence, Tool Development and Real-World Application, Explainability and Trust in AI Systems, Human-in-the-Loop Approaches, Evaluation and Benchmarking. The analysis examines their presence across stages, highlights the rise of LLM-assisted rule discovery, and identifies assurance practices. The review presents a stage-based gap analysis, an evidence-based agenda for interpretable, auditable, multimodal ACC, and a reproducible method for maintaining a living review over time.

abstract: Reliable crack assessment requires not only accurate pixel-level masks but also connected crack geometry and confidence estimates that remain stable under domain shift. However, existing segmentation models can achieve high overlap scores while fragmenting cracks, missing fine branches, and providing no calibrated uncertainty. To address this gap, this paper proposes CrackGeoFM, a multi-task framework that combines a frozen visual foundation backbone with crack-specific adaptation for mask prediction, skeleton reconstruction, and uncertainty estimation. The framework integrates a Frequency-Guided Crack Enhancement Module (FCEM) to enhance high-frequency crack cues, a Crack-Domain Feature Adaptation Module (CFAM) to adapt frozen backbone features to crack-domain patterns, and a Structure-Aware Multi-Task Decoder (SMTD) to jointly decode masks, skeletons, and uncertainty. Across 20 crack datasets, CrackGeoFM achieves state-of-the-art segmentation, improved topology preservation, calibrated uncertainty, and effective few-shot adaptation with only five labeled images. These results support reliable, generalizable, and engineering-oriented crack analysis for infrastructure assessment.

abstract: Dynamic life cycle assessment (DLCA) captures temporal changes for construction sector decision-making but faces challenges in modeling dynamics affecting embodied emissions, integrating multiple interacting factors, and providing transparent automated calculation methodologies. This paper introduces GraphDLCA, a tool embedding a building-sector DLCA database and, once the input parameters are defined, providing an automated calculation workflow for building DLCA. GraphDLCA supports automated hierarchical impact calculations from material to district. Four background dynamic factors are modeled: dynamic environmental impact calculation, dynamic import ratios, dynamic circular recycling/remanufacture, and dynamic electricity mix at three voltage levels. A proof of concept at different levels reveals that circular recycling/remanufacture lowers embodied impacts, while import ratios exert upward pressure. The dynamic electricity mix has limited influence on embodied emissions but pronounced effects on operational emissions from heating. GraphDLCA’s extensible architecture and transparent calculation logic provide a transferable foundation for future DLCA research and integration with digital construction workflows.

LLM-assisted quality-aware GA–multi-agent deep deterministic policy gradient framework for multi-robot collaborative scheduling in construction quality control
Automated dimension-aware BIM reconstruction from annotated floorplans through optimization-based text–geometry matching
abstract: Automated floorplan analysis is a critical foundation for generating building information models (BIMs) from two-dimensional (2D) floorplans, yet automation, reliable metric recovery, and engineering-level consistency remain insufficiently addressed. For raster floorplans, existing methods usually recover normalized or relative layouts rather than engineering-level metric parameters and are evaluated mainly with perception-oriented metrics, limiting their ability to reflect engineering applicability. To address this gap, this paper proposes a dimension-aware, optimization-based BIM reconstruction framework for annotated floorplans, in which optical character recognition (OCR)-derived dimensions are treated as localized metric constraints and explicitly linked to candidate geometric entities. The workflow integrates OCR-based text extraction, OCR-guided denoising, semantic segmentation, floorplan reconstruction, optimization-based text–geometry matching, and BIM generation. An Industry Foundation Classes (IFC)-based evaluation scheme is further introduced to assess geometric and metric consistency at the engineering level. Results show improved metric reliability and support automation-oriented BIM reconstruction.

title: Integrating vision-language model and point cloud processing for automated precast connection inspection and assembly optimization
Why floor plan object detection breaks under real scans: a controlled study of robustness limits
abstract: Robust object detection in architectural floor plans is essential for construction automation, yet real scans alter geometric depiction. This paper presents a controlled study based on CubiCasa5k, using paired CAD-derived and scanned raster images with identical layouts and annotations to isolate appearance. Three-seed RT-DETR experiments and Region-of-Interest composites separate object-region depiction shifts from background texture and clutter. Results show strongly class- and scale-dependent degradation: AP 75 and AP@0.85 deteriorate substantially more than AP 50 . Altered geometric depiction within object regions is the primary source of loss, whereas scanned backgrounds produce only a moderate decline. Single-run Faster R-CNN and RetinaNet checks show the same qualitative localization-loss signature without supporting detector ranking. Rather than introducing a new detector, this paper establishes a diagnostic benchmark and causal framework for robust detection of thin and small structures. The paired dataset variants, verification scripts, and trained checkpoints are publicly released. • Paired CubiCasa5k layouts isolate scan-induced depiction shifts. • ROI variants separate geometry depiction from scanned background effects. • Scan artifacts harm strict localization more than coarse detection. • Geometry depiction shifts dominate the performance loss. • Detector-family checks support the pattern; data and checkpoints are released.

Deep learning-based structural element extraction and knowledge-graph-based validation of 2D bridge drawings
abstract: The maintenance and management of existing bridge infrastructure rely on conventional two-dimensional construction drawings, which remain largely unstructured and difficult to integrate into digital workflows, including Building Information Modeling (BIM). In prestressed concrete bridges, tendons and anchorage systems are documented across multiple drawings and sectional views, making manual interpretation time-consuming and error-prone. This paper presents an automated pipeline for detecting and semantically structuring structural elements in 2D bridge drawings. The approach combines deep learning-based object detection, classical computer vision for identifier-frame detection, optical character recognition, and spatial matching to identify elements, recognize identifiers, and link elements with their labels. The extracted information is integrated into an ontology-based knowledge graph, enabling SPARQL-based validation of missing identifiers, cross-view relationships, and section-level quantities. On 29 bridge drawings, detection achieved mAP@50 values of up to 97.4%, and text recognition reached 93.0% exact-match accuracy with a 2.2% character error rate.

title: Vision-based prediction of seismic damage index for RC shear walls using morphological damage features
Automated pavement condition rating for cycle routes and greenways using deep learning
abstract: Active travel routes enhance sustainability, health, and safety while reducing environmental impact. Efficient maintenance of cycling infrastructure demands proactive pavement condition assessment. We present an intelligent pavement condition rating framework that utilises deep learning models for automated rating of offline cycleways using a GoPro mounted on the handlebar of a cycle. Firstly A novel rating scale, the Cycle Route Surface Index (CRSI), was developed specifically for cycleways\greenways in collaboration with Transport Infrastructure Ireland (TII) and used by domain experts from TII to manually annotate 43,594 greenway images. Secondly, deep learning models were then designed and enhanced to classify pavement conditions, outperforming traditional methods in both accuracy and speed. Thirdly, to increase trust in AI models, our framework incorporates transformer-specific Grad-CAM to explain predictions, enabling maintenance teams and planners to make informed, timely decisions. This proactive system improves greenway pavement conditions and shows strong potential for adoption in future urban cycleways.

title: Component-level BIM information extraction for steel-structure joints via multi-view recognition and graph-based relational encoding
Body-aware LiDAR framework for real-time excavator bucket pose estimation
IFC-based automated deconstructability analysis with market data integration through knowledge graphs
abstract: Deconstruction is vital for circular economy implementation in the construction sector, yet thin profit margins stifle its large-scale adoption. Consequently, deconstruction demands rigorous and data-driven planning. While Building Information Modeling (BIM) can serve this purpose, its readiness for deconstruction remains limited. This paper introduces DeconPlanner , a system that integrates Knowledge Graphs (KGs) and Industry Foundation Classes (IFC) to support digitally enabled deconstruction planning through two modules: an inference-based module that semantically enriches BIM with deconstruction sequencing; and an AI-powered market integration module that semantically enhances BIM by establishing semantic links between facility inventory and potential downstream stakeholders. Validation through a real-world case study demonstrated high performance for dependency inference (96.6% precision; 97.3% recall) and market integration (99.4% precision; 94% recall). Additionally, expert interviews confirmed the system's practicality and industry relevance. The findings demonstrate this framework's potential to reduce information fragmentation and establish the semantic foundation for future performance-based deconstruction workflows.

title: Contrastive boundary learning for automated quality inspection of shield tunnel segment assembly
Digital technologies for construction project delay mitigation: mechanism-based and scientometric framework
Predictive-comparative framework for construction cost control using long short-term memory and digital twin technologies
abstract: Fragmented project records and delayed validation hinder proactive cost control in construction. Yet current research offers limited guidance on converting inconsistent, lagged evidence into timely and auditable control signals, which can delay or complicate corrective action in practice. This paper develops a predictive-comparative framework integrating long short-term memory (LSTM) cost forecasting with digital twin (DT) progress verification for early cost governance. A sequence-to-sequence LSTM generates probabilistic cumulative cost trajectories, while the DT workflow reconstructs verified progress from digital models and translates it into cost-weighted earned value. Forecast, verified, and baseline curves are aligned on a monthly scale, and tolerance-based deviation filtering suppresses transient noise and flags sustained divergence. Synthetic experiments and a 24-month case study show strong alignment with realised cumulative costs and timely identification of sustained divergence. The framework provides a practical basis for cost governance and is extensible to live DT data streams and adaptive thresholds.

title: Editorial Board

Computer-aided architectural design for building façades: Systematic literature review
abstract: As building façade design becomes increasingly complex and requires consideration of multiple factors, the use of computational techniques has attracted substantial research interest. This paper presents a systematic literature review of computer-aided architectural design (CAAD) methods for building façades. A total of 133 articles published between 2015 and 2025 were analysed using quantitative and descriptive approaches. Based on the research methodologies employed, the applications of CAAD in façades can be categorised into three thematic groups: rule-based (12.4%), parametric/hybrid modelling (66.2%), and generative machine learning-based methods (21.4%). The analysis reveals the current research trends and highlights the strengths and limitations of different CAAD methods. To address the identified gaps in knowledge, future work is expected to integrate CAAD methods for complementary advantages, improve the transparency of CAAD methods, and leverage advanced computing technologies and interactive design patterns to improve design efficiency.

Understanding and modeling perceived cognitive and physical strain dynamics for planning-oriented human–robot collaboration in prefabricated construction
abstract: Human-robot collaboration (HRC) in prefabricated construction requires planning approaches that consider not only productivity but also time-dependent worker states during repeated work and rest. Existing planning models often rely on simplified assumptions about fatigue, workload, or recovery, with limited domain-specific empirical evidence on how perceived strain evolves. This study develops an empirically grounded, planning-oriented approach to characterize perceived strain accumulation and recovery in prefabricated construction HRC. A controlled repeated work-rest experiment assessed perceived cognitive and physical strain using the Rating Scale for Mental Effort and Borg's Rating of Perceived Exertion. Linear and exponential functional forms were evaluated, followed by mixed-effects modeling to examine collaborative conditions, session effects, and inter-individual variability. Results indicate that cognitive strain accumulation is best represented by a linear mixed-effects model, whereas rest-phase recovery follows nonlinear decay. The resulting planning-oriented models may inform future human-state-aware task allocation and scheduling research.

title: Contour-native bridge defect detection and compact digital archiving with Frequency-Supervised Fourier contours
abstract: AI-assisted bridge defect inspection often produces bounding boxes with crude geometry or raster masks that are costly to store, transmit, and reuse. This study investigates how detected defects can be represented as compact, recoverable contour-level vector records in image space. We propose Frequency-Supervised Fourier Series Detection (FS-FSD), which directly regresses Fourier contour descriptors and evaluates boxes, masks, and contours under a unified polygon-space protocol. On 3,767 UAV-collected bridge images with 42,346 defect instances, FS-FSD achieves higher polygon-space accuracy and better matched-TP geometric quality than representative detection, segmentation, and contour baselines. These results show that, compared with bounding boxes and raster masks, Fourier contour records preserve defect-boundary geometry in a more compact, recoverable, and shareable form for engineering review and downstream information workflows. Future work will study the modeling of multi-region, fragmented, and adjacent bridge-defect boundaries and extend the framework toward long-term bridge-defect tracking and lifecycle-oriented management.

title: Human-in-the-loop framework for automated IFC model validation and closed-loop quality management in BIM
Adaptive impedance control of wall-building robots in nonlinear viscoelastic environments using fuzzy wavelet neural networks and reinforcement learning
Integrating large language models for automated structural analysis
abstract: Automated analysis for engineering structures offers considerable potential for boosting efficiency by minimizing repetitive tasks. Although AI-driven methods are increasingly common, no systematic framework yet leverages Large Language Models (LLMs) for automatic structural analysis. This paper proposes a framework that employs domain-specific prompt design and in-context learning strategies to enhance LLM problem-solving capabilities and generative stability, enabling fully automated structural analysis from descriptive text to model outputs. A small-scale benchmark dataset consisting of 20 structural analysis word problems (SAWPs) is also introduced to evaluate the performance of different LLMs within the proposed framework. The results demonstrate that the proposed approach can increase the level of automation in solving SAWPs compared with traditional methods. Quantitatively, the framework built on GPT-5.4 and GPT-4o both achieved 100% accuracy, outperforming GPT-4 (85%), Gemini 1.5 Pro (80%), and Llama-3.3 (30%) on the test examples. Furthermore, integrating domain-specific instructions enhanced performance by 30% on problems with asymmetrical structural configurations.

title: Closed-loop digital twin framework with adaptive deformation prediction and risk assessment for automated deep excavations
Computational taxonomy development for digital passports using semantic topic modelling to advance circular construction
abstract: As circular economy principles become increasingly embedded in regulations, digital passports are being recognised as key enablers of circular construction. Although several digital passport concepts have been proposed, their implementation remains constrained by the lack of standardised, hierarchically structured data requirements. This paper presents a computational workflow that combines semantic topic modelling and unsupervised clustering to derive a common digital passport taxonomy from the state-of-the-art literature. To address inconsistencies in property names across data requirements, large language models are used to generate contextual property descriptions from the literature. Expert evaluation aligns moderately with cluster cohesion and diverges on hierarchical fit, indicating that statistically optimal taxonomies require manual moderation. The workflow can be used to semi-automatically generate and moderate taxonomies that structure disparate data requirements. This application can assist construction professionals in developing standardised digital passport data templates aligned with evolving regulations.

title: End-to-end framework for on-site rebar spacing measurement using deep learning and geometric reasoning
Robotic modular assembly in harsh environments: Framework-driven conceptual review
Discovery and prediction of tidal reach bridge scour morphology via 3D underwater sonar point cloud
Hybrid semantic segmentation framework for reinforced concrete bridge point clouds
abstract: Accurate point cloud segmentation is critical for the geometric BIM reconstruction of Reinforced Concrete (RC) bridges. However, existing approaches still face challenges in real-world applications, such as training data scarcity and poor generalisability. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a hybrid semantic segmentation framework, HyBridgeSeg, combining the strengths of both learning-based segmentation models and domain-knowledge-based segmentation rules. HyBridgeSeg decomposes the multi-class segmentation task into several tractable subtasks, each carefully designed with a segmentation pipeline. Validated on mixed synthetic-real and fully real-world datasets, HyBridgeSeg consistently outperformed its learning-based baselines. Hyb-PTv3 achieved the best performance on the mixed dataset, with 98.49% OA, 98.43% mPr, and 96.37% mIoU, while improving mIoU from 57.26% to 76.54% in synthetic-to-real validation and from 67.84% to 87.06% in real-to-real validation. These results confirm the accuracy, transferability, and potential of the hybrid strategy for bridge point cloud semantic segmentation.

title: Structure-oriented deep learning for semantic segmentation of bridge point clouds
abstract: Bridges built during the post-war construction boom are reaching the end of their design life, and their inspection still relies mainly on manual visual assessment. The specific question addressed is whether bridge components can be segmented accurately and efficiently from raw point clouds, without the manual denoising that existing methods require. This paper presents BridgeSeg, which combines a 12-dimensional structural feature embedding, a structure-aware encoder–decoder, and a loss constrained by the vertical hierarchy of bridge components, evaluated on three datasets covering 32 bridges. BridgeSeg reaches 96.6% mean intersection over union and 98.4% overall accuracy on unfiltered data, and reduces inference time by 89% compared with superpoint-based methods. This is significant for bridge owners and inspection engineers, since component-level segmentation becomes available on mainstream hardware and without preprocessing. The structure-oriented strategy can be extended to other infrastructure whose components follow known spatial rules.

title: Levels of automation in construction planning and control
abstract: To what extent should construction planning and control be automated, and where does added value emerge? This paper tested five automation levels in a digital twin construction (DTC) workflow for precast construction spanning factory, logistics, and site operations. A 1:25-scale residential building model controlled by a DTC system was used in a laboratory experiment with construction managers. Scenarios moved from monitoring to status interpretation, replanning recommendations, and plan commitment, with decision authority shifting incrementally from managers to system logic. Monitoring alone did not improve performance. Consistent directional improvements were observed after automation reached interpretation and recommendation, increasing average performance and reducing run-to-run dispersion. Autonomous commitment added little beyond decision support. The study shows that full autonomy is technically feasible in the testbed, although field-ready autonomy was not the primary objective. The main value threshold lies in interpretation and recommendation, indicating that these functions should be prioritized before autonomous plan commitment.

title: Scene-to-Twin: Just-in-time generation of fine-grained spatial models for multiscale digital twins in hydraulic construction
Automated optimization of visual sensor deployment for construction sites
Unified framework for robust Person Re-Identification in complex construction environments
Semantic-guided and geometry-enhanced training-free instance segmentation of bridge point clouds
Structural prior knowledge-guided point cloud classification of reinforced concrete bridge components
abstract: Accurate point cloud classification of bridge components is essential for Scan-to-BIM and semantic model reconstruction. However, existing learning-based methods rely mainly on data-driven feature learning and fail to capture bridge-specific structural characteristics. This paper, therefore, proposes a structural prior knowledge-guided method that incorporates bridge component distribution characteristics into point cloud classification. It combines (i) a bridge-wise batching strategy to preserve the component relationships within the same bridge with (ii) three bridge-specific structural prior knowledge constraints, namely elevation hierarchy, spatial adjacency, and projection overlap. Validated on 34 RC girder bridges, the proposed method consistently improved classification accuracy and convergence stability across different backbones and training-data settings, mitigated the synthetic-to-real domain gap, and achieved up to 99.1% OA and 98.3% mAcc with mixed synthetic-and-real training. These results highlight the value of incorporating scene-level structural prior knowledge into the processing of infrastructure point clouds.

title: Automated proximity monitoring and warning in construction: systematic review
LLM-enabled bidirectional material semantic alignment for automated BIM-to-building performance assessment
abstract: Integrating BIM material information into building performance assessment tools remains challenging, as IFC models often express material intent through project-specific names rather than analysis-ready thermophysical properties. This paper proposes Bidirectional Material Semantic Alignment (BMSA), a construction-context-aware semantic matching method within a two-stage framework that converts IFC material labels into hygrothermal-ready candidates. In Stage 1, BMSA applies LLM-based translation and enrichment to both IFC labels and reference entries to improve contextual material matching. Stage 2 ranks validated candidates using building physics, life cycle assessment, and life cycle cost criteria, with order-reversal checks to reduce LLM ranking bias. Evaluated on nine IFC models from six countries and five languages, the workflow achieved 90.8% candidate availability across 142 envelope labels, outperforming all lexical, neural, and LLM-enrichment baselines (+59 pp. over the strongest conventional baseline). Completed in 66 min at USD 4.20, the workflow demonstrates scalable, cost-effective automated BIM-to-building-performance assessment preparation.

title: Agentic search for BIM information extraction: Systematic evaluation
abstract: Although Building Information Models (BIM) help structure building data, retrieving specific information from them remains difficult for most project stakeholders. Natural-language (NL) interfaces can help mitigate this issue. Conventional approaches translate NL queries into structured queries that assume a fixed data organization, which BIM heterogeneity routinely invalidates. This paper addresses this limitation through agentic search, an LLM-based agent that iteratively retrieves information from BIM models while discovering their structure at runtime rather than relying on predefined assumptions. The approach is evaluated using ifc-bench v2, an open-source benchmark released with this work, comprising 1027 question–answer pairs across 37 IFC models. A 3 × 2 × 2 factorial experiment reveals that agentic search outperforms the static baseline in every configuration tested (+29.5 to +48.5pp). A detailed analysis uncovers the approach’s inner workings and remaining pitfalls, while a regression analysis ranks the factors driving accuracy: the search paradigm, followed by BIM-model quality and backbone capability.

title: In-situ 3D Concrete Printing of a Vaulted Ceiling Using a Mobile Robot
abstract: The geometric efficiency of vaulted ceilings makes them relevant to material-conscious construction, yet their automated in-situ fabrication remains challenging. This paper asks whether a mobile robot equipped for extrusion-based 3D concrete printing can accurately fabricate self-supporting vaults from below in spatially constrained environments through collision-free motions. The method combines layer-wise form-finding, onboard material supply, lightweight near-nozzle activation, redundancy-aware motion planning, and a print–drive–print workflow implemented with a mobile manipulator. Experiments establish feasibility: 14 full-scale vault segments up to 960 mm long were fabricated in approximately 15 min each, with laser scanning revealing standard layer-height deviations of around 0.5 mm. These findings provide architects, fabricators, and construction-robotics researchers with a basis for material-efficient ceiling fabrication in constrained construction and renovation contexts. They motivate research into continuous print-while-driving control, automated localization, cold-joint performance, structural testing, process robustness, and life-cycle impacts toward scalable in-situ construction under realistic site conditions.

title: RGB-D multimodal fusion perception-to-action system for automated detection and robotic sorting of construction and demolition waste
Comprehensive graph-based digital twin for correlation analysis of heterogeneous road infrastructure data
abstract: Predictive Maintenance (PM) of road infrastructure benefits from identifying trends and interactions in condition data through exploratory data analysis (EDA). However, road infrastructure data is typically heterogeneous, distributed, and managed across independent systems, limiting approaches that rely on centralized, homogenized data. Existing Digital Twin (DT) frameworks either lack scalability to entire road infrastructure systems or insufficiently capture diverse relationship types. This paper proposes a graph-based DT framework for scalable integration and analysis of heterogeneous road infrastructure data. Road infrastructure is represented as a System-of-Systems (SoS), with subsystems encoded as partially overlapping, schema-heterogeneous knowledge graphs. Spatial, temporal, and mereological relationships form dedicated subsystems, while distributed pattern matching enables cross-system data association. Evaluation using real-world German road infrastructure data demonstrates feasible cross-system integration and correlation analysis, while revealing limitations from incomplete and inconsistent legacy data. Synthetic experiments demonstrate scalability with increasing system size and complexity. Thus, the framework supports relationship-aware, data-driven analysis of heterogeneous and distributed road infrastructure systems.

title: Automatic measurement of rebar spacing on end faces of railway sleepers based on axial core-layer isolation and dual-prior constrained cylinder fitting

Toward autonomous infrastructure management: Agentic AI for structural health monitoring, robotics, and digital twins
Vision-encoder-integrated lifting tracker for cost-effective crane operations in modular construction
Exploiting structural repetition for synthetic training data generation in LiDAR point cloud segmentation
abstract: Maintaining aging tunnel infrastructure requires inspection supported by digital tools such as Building Information Models (BIMs). Scan-to-BIM methods based on deep learning automate BIM creation from Light Detection and Ranging (LiDAR) point clouds. However, supervised training requires large datasets that are costly to acquire. This paper presents an automatic synthetic data generation pipeline for subway tunnels. Tunnel segment meshes are assembled along stochastic 3D splines to generate 66.1 km of tunnel meshes, scanned by a LiDAR simulator to yield annotated point clouds. Data realism is assessed, and training strategies are benchmarked using three deep learning architectures evaluated on real-world tunnel scans. In certain cases, synthetic-only training outperforms training on small real datasets. Mixing synthetic and real data outperforms synthetic-only training, achieving 86.2% mIoU on real scans. The results demonstrate that synthetic data generation can reduce dataset creation costs, addressing a key barrier to the adoption of deep learning in construction. • A pipeline generates 66.1 km of annotated synthetic subway tunnel point clouds. • Synthetic data realism is assessed via segmentation with three deep learning architectures. • Synthetic-only training yields meaningful segmentation results despite domain gap. • Mixing in a small amount of real data achieves up to 86.2% mIoU on real scans. • Models generalize to unseen tunnel geometries.

title: Multi-robot cluster additive manufacturing: review of pathways, enabling technologies, and construction-aware deployment
Human-dominated or human-robot joint teams? Impact of human-robot collaboration modes on safety performance
Constructive AI: autonomous robotic 3D printing enabled by AI-driven process control and 3D machine vision
Vision-based assembly target pose estimation and adaptation for robotic assembly in Modular Integrated Construction
Adaptive task allocation and scheduling for human–robot collaborative construction under dynamic uncertainty
abstract: Human–robot collaborative (HRC) construction requires task allocation and scheduling that can accommodate changing site conditions while balancing duration and human fatigue. This paper examines how task representation, task–agent alignment, and rescheduling can jointly balance these objectives under dynamic uncertainty. A framework integrating directed acyclic graph generation from work breakdown structure, non-additive alignment, bi-objective optimization, and event-driven local repair is developed and evaluated using an interior finishing case with static baselines and repeated disruption experiments. Static optimization yielded distinct Pareto endpoints with a minimum makespan of 52.43 h and a minimum fatigue index of 0.89, while dynamic repair achieved the lowest mean fatigue index among the baselines (0.903) with a makespan of 58.04 h. These results help construction planners compare scheduling efficiency with human fatigue and adapt schedule quickly during disruptions. They motivate multi-trade field validation using worker-specific biomechanical measurements, site disruption records, and richer uncertainty and safety models.

title: Digital twins for building operation and maintenance: A scoping review (2019–2025)
abstract: Digital twins are increasingly used to automate building operation and maintenance (O&M). This scoping review synthesises 91 studies (2019–2025) to examine automated O&M tasks, data integration and synchronisation strategies, and key research gaps. Three recurring enablers are identified: semantic interoperability through ontologies and knowledge graphs, continuous calibration to maintain model fidelity, and stage-gated progression from advisory analytics to safeguarded closed-loop control. Human-centred themes include occupant comfort, indoor air quality, operator interfaces, extended-reality workflows, and governance for data provenance and emission claims. The review contributes an automation-oriented capability map from sensing to closed-loop actuation, codifies integration patterns that reduce manual configuration and support automated monitoring, and introduces readiness gates and assurance practices for safe, scalable, and auditable building automation.

title: Automating metal waste recovery in the construction lifecycle: vision-based deployment-oriented decision framework
abstract: Construction waste (CW) spans the entire construction lifecycle, yet CW automation lags behind circular construction objectives. Metals are the highest-value CW fraction, whereas offsite facilities can downgrade alloys into mixed bales through coarse ferrous/nonferrous separation and error-prone manual sorting. This paper develops a deployment-oriented decision framework mapping vision-based detector capabilities to distinct offsite sorting stages. To establish an empirical basis, WasteMetal-6 is introduced, a dataset of 2304 images and 35,787 object instances across six alloy classes under in-the-wild conditions. Eight detectors are evaluated under a hypothesis-driven framework: four state-of-the-art models, and four earlier-generation counterparts used for cross-architecture ablation. CNN-based models define the low-latency frontier while transformer-based models lead in material recovery. Four stage-specific decision criteria are derived, supporting real-time throughput exceeding 50 frames per second for primary screening. The resulting framework provides an evidence-based pathway for alloy-level metal recovery, supporting circular resource flows across the construction lifecycle.

title: Multi-paradigm simulation approach for building permit process optimisation
abstract: Coordinating multiple stakeholders in building permit processes is a complex challenge in construction management. This paper examines whether a multi-paradigm simulation approach can model and improve stakeholder coordination in such permit systems. A simulation framework combining agent-based modelling, system dynamics, and genetic algorithms is developed under a complex adaptive systems paradigm and validated against regulatory benchmarks and an empirical permit process structure. The model automates scenario evaluation through rule-based stakeholder behaviour, enabling computational analysis of coordination bottlenecks, performance trade-offs, and synchronisation effects. Findings highlight that treating building permit systems as adaptive coordination networks can improve regulatory performance under fixed structural conditions. The approach offers a foundation for simulation-based building permit process tools and research on automating governance processes in complex regulatory environments.
